items.title: beabadoobee Announces New Album Bananas 4 Cats, Reveals New Song “No Punctuation”: Stream
items.summary:
beabadoobee has announced a fifth album, Bananas 4 Cats, due February 19th through Dirty Hit and Interscope, and released its first single, "No Punctuation."

The announcement lands two months after Pylon, the album she put out in September. A press release frames the new record as "the yin to the yang of Pylon," with the two meant to show different sides of the same person. "I just needed to write an album like this after Pylon," beabadoobee said. "It happened naturally, I got back home and felt inspired, and made another album."

Home was the point of origin in a literal sense. As Consequence reported, she built the record in her London living room with a friend, her partner and her cats.

"No Punctuation" leans to the quieter end of her range, built on acoustic guitar and a soft vocal, a contrast to the rougher Pylon tracks "Sun Has Set" and "Switchblade." The lyrics stay plainly affectionate — "Just us two peas in a pod/ That's what we are," she sings, and later, "When I look around/ All I see is me and you/ Cause you are everything." The arrangement holds together until the final chorus, when the strings and guitars begin to slip out of alignment.

beabadoobee is currently working through the European leg of her Powerlines Tour. She heads to Asia for shows next spring and has a handful of festival dates abroad booked for summer 2027.

items.title: Tendo Nagenda Tapped As President Of Proximity Media
items.summary:
Proximity Media has hired Tendo Nagenda as its president. He starts November 30th and will oversee creative development and production across the company's film, television and nonfiction divisions, reporting to founders Ryan Coogler, Zinzi Coogler and Sev Ohanian.

Under the new structure, the heads of film, television and nonfiction report to Nagenda. He will work alongside Terra Potts, who handles marketing, operations and the In Proximity podcast, and co-founder Ludwig Göransson, who oversees music.

Nagenda comes to the job from a long run in studio and streaming development. He was vice president of original film at Netflix, where his slate included Da 5 Bloods, The Old Guard, Ma Rainey's Black Bottom, The Harder They Fall and Glass Onion, and before that executive vice president of production at Walt Disney Studios, covering live-action titles such as Beauty and the Beast, Cinderella, Mulan and Queen of Katwe. In 2022 he founded 10 by Ten Entertainment, whose first produced feature, Jeymes Samuel's The Book of Clarence, Sony released in January 2024.

"Tendo has spent his career working alongside talented filmmakers, championing original ideas and helping make projects that resonate with audiences around the world," the three Proximity founders said in a joint statement, per Deadline. Nagenda said he was "honored and excited to join Ryan, Zinzi, Sev and the entire Proximity team."

The hire follows a stretch of expansion for the company. Proximity produced Sinners, which took in more than $365 million worldwide, along with Creed III and Judas and the Black Messiah; its reimagining of The X-Files has a series greenlight at Hulu with Danielle Deadwyler and Himesh Patel attached, and it signed a multiyear television deal with Netflix covering scripted and unscripted work. Its nonfiction slate includes National Geographic's Hurricane Katrina: Race Against Time, the network's most-watched U.S. streaming title, plus Stephen Curry: Underrated, Homeroom and Anthem.

items.title: Phoebe Bridgers – “Anything” (Adrianne Lenker Cover)
items.summary:
Phoebe Bridgers has released a cover of Adrianne Lenker's "Anything," reviving a holiday-season tradition she had let lapse. Bridgers and Lenker are both donating their proceeds from the single to the Palestine Children's Relief Fund.

Lenker first released "Anything" as the lead single from her 2020 album songs. Bridgers co-produced her version with Jack Antonoff, Tony Berg and Ethan Gruska, all frequent collaborators, and the recording samples Lenker's original. Angela Deane supplied the cover art, a callback to Bridgers' debut Stranger in the Alps.

The annual holiday cover had been a fixture of Bridgers' release calendar for years, with entries including the Handsome Family's "So Much Wine" in 2022 and "The Parting Glass" with boygenius and Irish folk duo Ye Vagabonds in 2023. As Stereogum noted, the tradition appeared to have ended after that. Her take on "Anything" keeps the fragility of Lenker's version while adding a fuller, more produced arrangement.

The cover arrives during a busy stretch. Bridgers' Lost Weekend is nominated for Album of the Year at the Grammys, she recently extended her no-phones arena tour and played Saturday Night Live, and she made her acting debut in Lance Oppenheim's Primetime, for which she recorded the end-credits song "On Video." That track was her first new music since Lost Weekend; "Anything" is her second.
